Scaramucci insists BTC must break $100,000: the bear market is almost over—there’s only one reason
Skybridge Capital’s founder remains bullish, believing that the post-halving supply contraction will drive the next major surge.

Scaramucci (yes, the former White House communications director who served there for 11 days—now CEO of Skybridge Capital) has once again publicly stated that BTC will break $100,000. His core logic is only one thing—the supply contraction caused by the halving cycle. After each halving, miners’ selling pressure is cut in half, so there is less new supply for the market to absorb. Historically, several major bull runs have followed this pattern. Notably, the timing of when he made this call is exactly when BTC’s volatility has compressed into an extremely narrow range. At present, BTC is $69,288.01, up 7.42% over the past 24 hours.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Celebrity trading calls themselves are emotional fuel. BTC is already up 7%+ today, while ETH is up even more—17.70% to $2,254.14. Overall market risk appetite has clearly rebounded, and such remarks will strengthen the bullish narrative.
- Medium term: If the halving thesis plays out, the key variable is continued inflows of institutional capital. The Wall Street voice represented by Scaramucci matters because it provides psychological endorsement for institutional investors to enter.

My take

SharpLink’s single-quarter loss of $394 million, while ETH surged 18%: does the paper loss really scare? 

SharpLink, a major ETH holder, reported a Q2 loss of $394 million—almost entirely non-cash, mark-to-market accounting losses on its ETH position—yet the price of ETH rose 18% in a single day.

SharpLink, an Ethereum treasury strategy firm, released its Q2 results: net loss of $394.3 million. But if you look at the breakdown, the bulk comes from two parts: paper losses from marking its ETH holdings to market, plus impairment of liquid staking tokens (LSTs). In plain terms, accounting rules require that at the end of each quarter, the holdings be revalued based on the prevailing prices. When ETH falls, the books must record losses—even though no coins in the wallet have actually been sold.

One-sentence translation: it’s not that operations lost money; it’s just that in Q2, ETH’s price was lower, so the accounting figures look ugly.

Impact on the market
- Short term: sentiment is somewhat bearish. Retail investors who don’t know the full story may panic at the “huge loss” headline, but in reality there’s no real selling pressure. ETH is trading at $2,263.36, up 18.21% over the last 24 hours, and the market has effectively voted with its feet, ignoring the report. BTC is also above $69,514.52, up 7.72%.
- Medium term: the stock prices and financial reports of these ETH treasury companies will continue to be tied to crypto prices, with volatility amplified. When institutions see billion-level accounting swings in a single quarter, they’ll be more cautious in valuing the ETH treasury model, and fundraising becomes harder.

My take
I classify this earnings report as “scary numbers, fundamentally neutral.” The loss is non-cash; the core variable is only ETH’s price itself. Today’s 18% surge in ETH shows that control of the capital is driven by the market, not the report. Watch whether $2,263 can hold. If it breaks, the paper loss will likely expand further in the next quarter and sentiment will turn bearish; if it holds, the report will be digested quickly. I lean toward staying on the sidelines but slightly bullish; the risk is the momentum of follow-the-news selloffs around earnings season.

- Short term: Institutions use proxy assets to go long with leverage, effectively putting a “multiplier” on BTC. Clearly bullish. The volume structure shows this round isn’t retail FOMO—institutions are really deploying capital, and they’re doing it through the stock market, a “formal” channel. After BTC breaks above $69,528, as long as MSTR’s trading volume doesn’t fall, this trend isn’t over. In a new report, BlackRock believes the long-term investment logic for BTC after the drawdown hasn’t changed, and maintains the 1–2% allocation recommendation for a portfolio.

BlackRock released a report titled “Re-Underwriting Bitcoin.” The core message is essentially this: although BTC has retreated more than 50% from its October 2025 peak, the investment case for the asset itself is still intact. They continue to recommend allocating 1–2% from the stock allocation to BTC. Note their wording is “re-underwriting”—as if they have re-evaluated BTC from top to bottom after the selloff, with the conclusion that the ruling hasn’t changed. Now, at the moment when the global largest asset manager (managing over $10 trillion) is publicly endorsing it during the bleakest market conditions, the timing alone speaks volumes.

Impact on the market
- Short term: A positive boost to sentiment. Current BTC is at $69,430, up 7.31% in 24 hours. ETH is even more dramatic at $2,254, up 17.63% on the day. After the halving-style drawdown, institutions openly saying “the long-term logic is intact” provides an official excuse for sidelined capital to re-enter. But honestly, the report doesn’t change near-term supply/demand—whether it rises or falls still depends on capital flows.
- Medium term: BlackRock’s IBIT is the largest BTC spot ETF issuer. Since it doesn’t reduce its allocation recommendation, it implies the narrative of ongoing ETF inflows is still there. A halving-style drawdown hasn’t changed the institutional allocation framework—this is more meaningful than any one-off trading call.

One-sentence translation: BlackRock has re-calculated the books for BTC after the drawdown, and the conclusion is that this “stock” can still be held.

Bullish, but in stages. BlackRock’s endorsement plus a 7% rebound in one day suggests that bottom-anchoring demand is real. BlackRock issues a call: BTC is down 50% from the highs, but still recommends allocating 1–2%

In its new report, “Re-Underwriting Bitcoin,” BlackRock says the 50% drawdown hasn’t changed the long-term logic, maintaining its 1–2% allocation recommendation.

BTC has retraced more than 50% from its October 2025 peak. It is currently at $69,430, up 7.31% over the past 24 hours. However, the world’s largest asset manager, BlackRock, released a report titled “Re-Underwriting Bitcoin,” and the core message is essentially this: even after a 50% drop, the investment logic remains the same.

Their suggested portfolio allocation is still 1–2%, and the position should be shifted out of equities rather than funded with fresh capital. In plain terms: BlackRock is treating the selloff as an opportunity to reassess—after reviewing, they found the conclusion is still the same as before.

Impact on the market
- Short term: This is a classic confidence “floor” signal. When an institution managing assets worth $10 trillion publicly says “a 50% drop doesn’t change the logic,” it directly offsets panic sentiment. Today, BTC rebounded 7.31% and ETH rose 17.63%, indicating the market itself is already repairing; BlackRock’s comments land while the rebound is in progress, effectively delivering ammunition to the bulls.
- Medium term: The 1–2% allocation guidance is being transferred from stocks, implying BlackRock sees BTC as a substitute/diversifying asset for equities—not a safe-haven asset. If this framework is adopted by more institutions, the logic of BTC’s correlation with the Nasdaq will likely be further reinforced. Rate-cut expectations plus equity market liquidity remain its main engines.

My view
Clearly bullish. The logic is simple: after a 50% drawdown, the biggest institutional holder—after completing new due diligence—chose to maintain its stance rather than cut positions, which carries far more weight than just issuing a trading call. BTC is stabilizing above $69,000; ETH’s 17.63% intraday elasticity suggests capital is flowing back into risk assets. The risk is that BlackRock’s 1–2% is a long-term framework and doesn’t mean BTC won’t test lows again in the short term. If the macro environment worsens, this recommendation won’t rescue the weekly timeframe. But in terms of direction, institutions haven’t retreated—this is the most important signal for the bottom area.

One-sentence translation: After the drop by half, they redo due diligence and the conclusion is still “worth allocating to,” which is more convincing than hype when prices are up.

title: 同样是利好，为什么有些信息能够在很短时间内改变市场行为？？
subTitle:
过去 24 小时出现了一个很有意思的现象：政策制定者、监管者、交易平台负责人、机构和真实市场行为同时在向 Crypto 市场释放不同层级的信号。
⸻
过去 24 小时，加密市场出现了一个很值得研究的现象。
美国总统特朗普在白宫与 Coinbase、Robinhood、Ripple、Kraken 等加密行业高管会面，并再次公开推动国会通过 CLARITY Act，希望进一步明确美国数字资产监管框架。与此同时，SEC、CFTC 等监管层的政策动作也成为市场关注焦点。
随后，Bitcoin 一度上涨超过 6%，突破 68,000 美元；Coinbase、Strategy、Circle 等 Crypto 相关股票也出现明显上涨。
如果只从行情角度看，很容易得出一个简单结论：
“政策利好 → BTC 上涨。”
但从 Market Expectation Systems 的角度，我更感兴趣的是另一个问题：
为什么这类信息能够在很短时间内改变市场行为？
答案可能并不只在“消息内容”。还在于：
谁在说。谁在行动。以及这些信号之间是否形成了相互验证。
⸻
01｜同一句话，由不同的人说，市场赋予的权重不同
假设一个普通 Crypto KOL 说：
“美国正在变得更加 Crypto Friendly。”
这是一个观点。
如果 Coinbase CEO 说类似的话，市场可能会提高一点权重。
如果 SEC 或 CFTC 的负责人开始讨论新的监管框架，它就从观点进一步变成：
制度信号。
而如果美国总统在白宫公开推动数字资产立法，市场对这条信息的解释权重又会发生变化。
因为市场会判断：
这个信息源是否拥有改变现实的能力？
所以信息的影响力不能只写成：
Information → Expectation
更准确的表达可能是：
Information × Source Credibility × Decision Power → Expectation Impact
⸻
02｜“身份”本身，就是信号的一部分
这也是为什么市场预期管理不能只研究：
说了什么。
还必须研究：
谁说的。
不同角色天然承担不同功能：
政治人物可以改变政策预期。
监管机构可以改变制度确定性。
交易平台能够提供市场基础设施信号。
项目创始人能够解释战略意图。
研究者能够帮助市场解释复杂机制。
KOL能够影响注意力和认知扩散。
机构的资金行为则能够提供另一种完全不同的信号：
Skin in the Game。
也就是：你不仅这样认为，
你真的因此采取了行动。
⸻
03｜“说”和“做”，市场给予的权重也不同
这是我认为今天特别值得观察的一点。
如果一个机构公开说：“我们长期看好 Bitcoin。”这是 Narrative Signal。
如果它随后真正配置 Bitcoin，就出现了：
Behavioral Signal。
如果越来越多不同类型机构都出现类似行为，市场得到的就不再只是一个观点。而是：
行为证据。
同样，一个巨鲸说看好某项资产是一件事；链上真正发生大额买入，是另一件事。
项目宣布用户增长是一件事；链上用户真的持续增加，又是另一件事。
所以市场会不断比较：
Narrative 和 Behavior 是否一致？
⸻
04｜但巨鲸买入，也不能直接等于“强信号”
这里非常容易产生另一个误区。看到：某机构买入，某巨鲸买入，某知名人物看多。就立刻认为：这是重大利好。其实不够。
因为行为同样需要解释：
一个钱包转移 1 亿美元资产，可能是买入，也可能是内部资金调整，可能是托管迁移，也可能准备进入交易平台。所以我们不能看到链上大额转账，就直接把它解释成：“Whale is bullish。”
Market Expectation Systems 更关心的是：
Source
↓
Intent
↓
Action
↓
Context
↓
Confirmation
只有这些信息逐渐对齐，行为信号的可信度才会上升。
⸻
05｜真正强的市场信号，往往来自“交叉验证”
回到过去24小时。
真正值得研究的，并不是某一个人说了什么。而是不同类型信号开始同时出现：
政治层。释放政策方向。
↓
监管层。讨论具体规则。
↓
行业层。Coinbase、Robinhood、Ripple、Kraken 等核心参与者直接参与政策讨论。
↓
资本市场。Coinbase、Strategy、Circle 等相关股票上涨。
↓
Crypto市场。Bitcoin 快速上涨，并出现大规模空头清算；报道显示短时间内强制平仓进一步放大了价格运动。
这时候，市场面对的就不再是：
一个人的观点。
而是：
多个不同角色产生的信号开始相互验证。
⸻
06｜这正是 Market Expectation Systems 关注的问题
一条完整的预期形成路径可能是：
Official Signal
↓
Authoritative Source
↓
Interpretation
↓
Third-party Validation
↓
Behavioral Evidence
↓
Market Reaction
↓
Expectation Update
这和单纯做一次 KOL Campaign，是完全不同的逻辑。
⸻
07｜对 Web3 项目方尤其重要
假设一个项目完成了一次重大技术升级。
最简单的方式是：
项目官方发布公告。
然后几十个 KOL 转发。
但 Market Expectation Systems 会进一步拆解：
官方、创始人、技术研究者、生态合作伙伴、用户和开发者、链上数据
构建成一条完整的：
Evidence Chain。
⸻
08｜所以，真正重要的不是“找谁喊得最大声”
很多项目拥有非常大的 KOL List。但这并不意味着它拥有：
Expectation Network。
100个账号同时说同一句话，市场很容易识别这是 Campaign。
真正成熟的市场预期系统应该让：不同身份，不同利益关系，不同专业能力，不同可信度来源，围绕同一个事实提供不同层面的验证。最终市场自己得出结论。
这时候形成的预期，通常比单纯重复更加稳定。
⸻
09｜这也是我们为什么会对 KOL 进行“功能分类”
我们更关注：
这个人在市场预期形成过程中承担什么功能？
有人擅长制造：
Attention。
有人拥有：
Interpretation Power。
有人能够在社区内部持续完成：
Community Reinforcement。
还有一些人真正重要的地方是：
Credibility。
因为目标市场相信：
“在这个问题上，他有资格解释。”
所以：
Follower ≠ Influence
Influence ≠ Credibility
Credibility ≠ Conversion
这是三个完全不同的问题。
⸻
10｜市场真正形成新预期的时候
并不是所有人突然说出了同一句话。而是：越来越多彼此相对独立的参与者，基于自己掌握的信息和真实行为，开始得出相似的判断。
于是：
Signal
↓
Credibility
↓
Interpretation
↓
Validation
↓
Behavior
↓
Expectation Update
开始形成。
这也是过去24小时市场给我的一个很好的现实观察：
市场不会平等对待每一个声音。
身份决定初始权重，行为提供真实验证，而多个独立信号的一致性，才可能真正改变市场预期。
所以，Market Expectation Systems 真正设计的，
从来不只是：
“谁帮项目发内容。”
而是：
谁应该在什么时间，以什么身份，提供哪一层信息、解释和验证，让市场最终形成自己的判断。
这才是我理解的：
Expectation Formation。

不是投资建议，仅作为市场机制与行业观察。

#termmax @termmax  Recently @termmax  used the Binance Booster launched on August 17 to push a strong wave of promotion. Throwing resources at attracting users is understandable, but rather than opening up another traffic channel, what should actually be done now is to refine the whole path for newcomers to "enter, borrow, leverage, and safely exit" so it feels more grounded. The more stuff gets crammed in, the easier it is for retail users to have no idea what they are randomly clicking.

TermMax is no longer the pure product it once was. Just look at V2: aggregation routing, limit orders, and a position dashboard have all been added, and the interface is packed with a bunch of public chains such as Ethereum, Arbitrum, BNB Chain, Base, and HyperEVM. A full-featured setup certainly shows technical strength, but the drawbacks are also obvious: when ordinary users go in, they have to instantly digest multiple chains, asset types, settlement cycles, fixed-income algorithms, collateral ratios, and the complex GT/FT token logic before they can nervously choose between lend, borrow, or leverage.

Experienced users may think this is all normal, but if the goal is a product for the masses, this barrier is a real problem. I still can’t forget that absurd incident from back then: because the UI wasn’t finished, the official team actually wrote a long article teaching everyone to use Etherscan to interact with the contract and force settlement with FT. That shows a simple reality: no matter how smoothly the backend code runs, if the frontend doesn’t hold things together, the experience is a fail.

Nowadays the homepage is still fixated on "one-click leverage," but I feel that misses the point: getting into a position with one click is great, but if I want to exit early, or I enter the wrong parameters by mistake, can the system make it crystal clear in one second how to fix it? The real power of DeFi is not in wrapping tons of complicated logic into a flashy button, but in leaving retail users a simple, straightforward way out when something goes wrong, so they can safely get their money back themselves. #eth $ETH

#termmax @termmax  I’m just going to say what’s on my mind. I’ve been watching the Binance Booster campaign that TermMax launched on August 17, and I can’t help feeling a bit uneasy. The project team is doing everything they can to find channels to drive traffic and attract new “fresh lettuce.” There’s nothing wrong with that. But the more they keep adding features, the easier it becomes for ordinary players to get “lost.” Instead of rushing to open new doors, I think the most urgent thing to fill is the gap in polishing the entire process—borrowing, leveraging, and then liquidating and exiting—making it as minimal and streamlined as possible, so it doesn’t keep testing people’s intelligence.

Look at TermMax now—this isn’t the same straightforward fixed-rate lending/borrowing tool from before. The V2 version has turned into a full-on grab bag of functions: unified routing, limit orders, and a position dashboard, all in one. When you open the app, Ethereum, Arbitrum, BNB Chain, Base, and HyperEVM line up like a menu. It looks big and comprehensive, but the pain points come right along with it. A random user walks in and suddenly has to instantly absorb the network environment, asset types, maturity date, fixed yield rate, and collateral ratio—on top of needing time to understand the GT/FT token mechanics—before they can finally, clumsily, choose whether to lend, borrow, or leverage.

The old-timers might think this kind of operation is pretty normal. But if the vision is to build a financial product for the masses, then these steps are stacked way too high. I still clearly remember a pretty ridiculous incident: back when the UI wasn’t updated yet, TermMax’s official team actually posted a hardcore guide teaching users, step by step, to go to Etherscan and manually rebalance using FT after adjusting the contract. That perfectly illustrates a simple truth: code that runs is one thing—whether it’s “usable” in the hands of real users is completely another.

Nowadays, the website is full of “one-click leverage” as a selling point, but I’m honestly not very impressed by it. One-click opening is certainly smooth. The question is: if I change my mind halfway and want to exit early, or if I accidentally click the wrong thing, will the system provide the same kind of clear, intuitive “first-aid” guidance? The real barrier in DeFi has never been hiding all the backend complexity behind a button. It’s whether—when the situation becomes complicated—it still lets retail users move their funds out safely and clearly. #eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  I’ve been re-examining the logic behind @Dusk_Foundation  over and over. Honestly, the biggest worry has never really been whether “real-world assets can be tokenized on-chain.” The real problem is this: even if this grand plan succeeds, what gives $DUSK  the right to take a cut?

The official headline achievements really are impressive. If you look through the Dusk website, you can see metrics like “€300M+ confirmed issuance,” “50K+ investor reach,” and “210M+ DUSK staked.” Then by August 15, the team further expanded the tokenization narrative into the SME (small and medium-sized enterprise) private placement market. Along with that, Dusk Trade is also working hard to open the doors to regulated financial product trading—stocks, bonds, funds, and more. The level of detail in business execution is visibly getting finer.

But when you return to the economic model itself, the logic chain is still disconnected.

At present, the only rigid use cases for DUSK are basically two things: serving as network fuel (gas) and node staking. What’s hard to understand is that the fees generated on-chain aren’t burned via a deflationary mechanism; instead, they’re put back into block rewards. Even worse, the protocol is planning to release a full 500 million DUSK tokens over the next 36 years. Looking just at the first four years, that corresponds to as much as about 250.48 million newly created token sell-pressure, and within that output, 10% is forcibly allocated to the development fund.

This leads to the most fundamental contradiction:

Suppose that in the future, hundreds of millions of euros worth of off-chain assets are truly moved onto the chain. Traditional syndicates would only treat this as a purely underlying channel. Other than paying extremely cheap gas fees with their noses held shut, investors have no reason at all to buy on the secondary market and lock tokens long-term. In other words, “fundamentals expansion” and “token price appreciation” are being forcibly severed.

So although the 210M+ staking number looks prosperous on the surface, I can’t help but be skeptical: how much of it is actually driven by genuine underlying operational demand? And how much is purely to capture that emission (inflationary output)? We need to face reality: the willingness to lock tokens built by unlimited money-printing is simply not on the same dimension as the willingness to hold tokens supported by real commercial profit.

So right now, I really hope the official can adjust the messaging they put out externally—stop drawing those vague, distant grand promises. #eth $ETH

官方明面上的成绩确实亮眼。去翻看 Dusk 官网，“€300M+ confirmed issuance”、“50K+ investor reach”还有“210M+ DUSK staked”这些指标都赫然在列。到了 8 月 15 日，团队又进一步铺开了 SME（中小企业）私募市场的代币化叙事。与之配套，Dusk Trade 也在全力打通股票、债券、基金等合规金融产品的交易大门。业务推进的颗粒度肉眼可见地变细了。

可是，一回归到经济模型本身，逻辑链条还是脱节的。

当下 DUSK 仅有的刚性应用场景无非两点：充当网络燃料（gas）和节点质押（staking）。让人费解的是，链上产生的手续费并没有采取通缩销毁机制，反而被重新塞进了出块奖励里。更要命的是，协议甚至规划了未来 36 年还要释放足足 5 亿枚 DUSK。单看头 4 年，就对应着高达约 2.5048 亿枚的新增抛压，而且这部分产出里还有 10% 被硬性划归给了 development fund。

这就引出了最核心的矛盾：

假设未来真有数以亿计欧元的圈外资产搬到了链上，传统财团也只不过是把这里当成个纯粹的底层通道。除了捏着鼻子支付极其低廉的 gas 费用外，资方根本没有任何去二级市场扫货、长期锁仓的理由。也就是说，“基本面扩张”跟“币价拉升”被硬生生割裂了。

那 210M+ 的质押数字表面看着繁荣，但我始终保持怀疑：这其中有多少属于真实的底层运转诉求？又有多少纯粹是为了套取那个 emission（通胀产出）？我们要认清现实，靠无节制印钞堆出来的锁仓量，与靠真实商业利润支撑的持币意愿，根本不在一个维度。

所以，我现在极其希望官方能调整一下对外宣发的口径，少去画那些虚无缥缈的大饼。#eth $ETH

Trump Announces an “Economic D-Day” for Iran, Threatens Secondary Sanctions Too—Is This Rally in BTC $69,344 Unrealistic?

💡 Impact Assessment: Bearish. Escalating geopolitical tensions plus the risk of sanctions spreading may cause risk-averse funds to pull out of crypto.

First, the current situation: BTC is now at $69,344, up 7.23% over the past 24 hours; ETH is at $2,249.67—even stronger, up 17.47%. But at this point in time, don’t get too excited: bulls may be premature.

One sentence to make it clear
Trump has signaled a crackdown on Iran with “Economic D-Day” level sanctions, and warned that third parties who do business with Iran will also be hit by secondary sanctions. This directly shocks global risk assets, and BTC is the first to be hit.

What’s going on
Trump publicly announced an escalation of economic sanctions on Iran, calling the intensity “Economic D-Day,” meaning a comprehensive encirclement like the Normandy landings. More importantly is “secondary sanctions”—not only sanctioning Iran itself, but also countries and companies that continue buying oil from Iran or doing trade with it, which would be kicked out of the U.S. financial system. In plain terms, it’s forcing the world to take sides. The issue is that Iran’s main buyers for crude oil include several major economic powers. If this is executed, oil prices, shipping, and supply chains will all have to shake. This kind of news is a double blow to the crypto market: on one hand, geopolitical conflict suppresses risk appetite; on the other, dollar liquidity may tighten due to the knock-on effects of sanctions.

Market impact
- Short term: This 7%+ surge in BTC happened as traders front-ran before the sanction details were released. Once the specifics are published, there could be significant pressure to give back gains. ETH is up 17.47%—the stronger it rises, the harder it may fall when geopolitical negatives arrive.
- Medium term: Secondary sanctions may freeze some offshore USD liquidity. Historically, every time large-scale sanctions are rolled out, stablecoin settlement volumes and OTC trading tend to get restless first, then contract—overall acting like a slow drain on market depth.

My take
I’m bearish in the short term. At the $69,344 level, the prior 7% rally has essentially already priced in higher risk appetite. Geopolitical “black swan” news is most likely to trigger leveraged liquidation cascades when prices are high. Support to watch is around the $66,000 area—if that breaks, most of this rally’s gains will likely be given back. ETH at $2,249.67 faces similar pullback risk after a 17% rise; around $2,050 is the first line of defense. Of course, there’s another scenario: sanctions are not as severe as expected—if it’s more “rumor, not reality” (big noise, small impact)—the market could repair quickly. But before details are confirmed, holding long positions overnight is clearly higher risk. This level is more suitable for watching than chasing.

One-line translation: This Iran story isn’t about firing missiles—it’s about taking aim at the dollar settlement network, and the crypto market fears liquidity being drained the most.

- 短期：BTC这波7%+的涨幅是在消息落地前抢跑的，制裁细节一旦公布，获利盘回吐压力不小。ETH涨了17.47%，涨得越猛，地缘利空来了摔得越狠。
- 中期：二级制裁会冻结部分离岸美元流动性，历史上每次大规模制裁落地，稳定币结算量和场外交易都会先躁动后收缩，对市场深度是慢性抽水。

我的判断
我短期看空。BTC在$69,344这个位置，前面7%的涨幅等于提前透支了风险偏好，地缘黑天鹅消息最容易在高位引发杠杆清算连锁。下方盯住$66,000一线的支撑，破了这波涨幅基本回吐完。ETH $2,249.67同样面临17%涨幅的回踩风险，$2,050附近是第一道防线。当然，也存在另一种情景：制裁落地不及预期、雷声大雨点小，那市场会快速修复。但在细节公布前，拿着多头仓位过夜的风险明显偏高，这个位置更适合观望而不是追高。

Ukrainian drones blew up a Russian oil refinery—oil prices skyrocketed, so why did BTC at $69,329 actually benefit?

💡 Impact assessment: Bullish. Escalation of war → higher energy prices → increased demand for inflation hedges → capital flows into hard assets like BTC.

How it happened
Ukraine intensified its drone strikes on Russia’s oil refineries and oil depots, directly hitting the other side’s energy lifeline and causing a fuel shortage inside Russia. Instead of targeting armies, these strikes hit the “economic ability to generate blood”—oil export revenue is a pillar of Russia’s fiscal budget. The conflict pattern has shifted from fighting for territory to dismantling infrastructure. As a result, global energy market supply expectations tighten immediately, putting upward pressure on oil prices.

Market impact
- Short term: As geopolitical tensions escalate, traditional risk assets may initially shake, but the transmission mechanism is different this time: oil prices rise → inflation expectations heat up → concerns about fiat purchasing power → funds seek hard-asset safe havens. BTC is currently at $69,329.19, up 7.21% in 24 hours; ETH at $2,251.78 is up even more, by 17.65%. The market is voting with its feet. On-chain and ETF fund flows provide direct support for prices, not emotional “call-and-signal” trading.
- Medium term: With the conflict likely to drag on and the global energy price center of gravity rising, the risk of global stagflation increases. This actually strengthens the “digital gold” narrative for BTC. Historically, after geopolitical black swans, discussions about BTC’s safe-haven characteristics tend to heat up.

My take
I’m bullish, but not blindly bullish. At the $69,329 level, there’s short-term profit-taking pressure. If a pullback toward the $67,000 area stabilizes, the trend structure won’t be broken. ETH’s rally of 17.65% outperformed BTC, suggesting that risk appetite has returned. The risk is that if the conflict de-escalates quickly, the safe-haven premium could unwind—fast gains can also come with fast drops. Volatility in geopolitics-driven markets is high; position management matters more than directional prediction.

title: U.S. Crypto Regulation Takes Center Stage as Bitcoin Surges$
subTitle:
The U.S. crypto industry is back in the spotlight as policymakers push toward clearer rules for digital assets.
At a White House crypto event, President Donald Trump called on Congress to move forward with the CLARITY Act, a major piece of legislation aimed at creating a clearer regulatory framework for the crypto market. The bill is facing political and industry hurdles, so its final outcome remains uncertain.

Meanwhile, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has proposed a new framework that could create specific exemptions and clearer pathways for certain crypto offerings. The proposal is now open for public comment.
The regulatory developments came as the crypto market experienced a sharp rally. Bitcoin moved above $68,000, while Ethereum climbed back above $2,000. More than $1 billion in short positions were liquidated during Bitcoin’s surge, adding to the market’s momentum.

For crypto investors and businesses, the bigger question is whether clearer U.S. regulations could encourage more institutional participation and long-term adoption.
